items.title: Google Search What People Are Saying AI-Generated Emojis
items.description: Google seems to be placing emojis in the AI-generated "What people are saying" box in Google Search. Google does show emojis in its search results, but these emojis are not coming from the website it is referencing, but rather from Google Search and its AI-generated descriptions.

items.title: Google Hotel Search Listings With Continue On Google To Book
items.description: Google seems to be rolling out hotel booking directly on Google in Google Search but through AI Mode. So when you search on Google and Google shows you the hotels, you can now click on a button that says "Continue on Google" and it then takes you through the AI Mode hotel booking feature to book using your Google account.

items.title: Google Search Tests "Show Original Results" Button
items.description: Google Search is testing a new button in the search results named "Show original results." It seems this button does something similar to the "Search instead for" link, where Google will auto correct or adapt your query when it thinks you have a typo in your query or you meant to search for something else.

items.title: Google Data Feed Validation Tool Has Been Turned Down
items.description: Google has "turned down" its Data Feed validation tool and has removed references to it from the Book actions (Book) structured data help documentation. I am not sure when this tool surfaced but likely sometime between October 2016 and December 2017 alongside the broader Actions on Google developer platform.

items.title: Google Images Results With Lens To AI Mode Feature
items.description: Google image search results now let you click a Google Lens button, which takes you into an AI Overview follow-up query or even an AI Mode follow-up query. This is different from when Google added the Google Lens button to image search results.

items.title: Supporting a shared AI training control for websites
items.description: Today, we're announcing our plans to support a shared AI training control in robots.txt. This will help websites express their AI training preferences across multiple AI providers in a single step and is based on work from the AIPREF working group at the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). This builds on our long history of providing website owners with clear controls, including through Google-Extended, the AI training control we've offered since 2023.

items.title: New learning paths: curated YouTube playlists for Search fundamentals and Technical SEO
items.description: Over the years, the Search Central YouTube channel has published hundreds of videos across various series, from Search for Beginners and Ask Googlebot to Search Console Training and Search Off the Record. While our series structure works well for deep dives and episodic updates, we know that finding a clear, sequential learning path from scratch can sometimes be challenging.

items.title: Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console
items.description: Understanding how users find your content is crucial for any publisher or site owner. As Search evolves to include more visual and multimodal experiences, we want to ensure you have the data you need to analyze your performance.

items.title: Update to the Site Reputation Policy
items.description: In 2024, we introduced our site reputation policy to stop a practice where third-party content is published on a trusted website just to exploit that site's good reputation to rank higher in Search. This practice hurts search quality, and creates a bad experience for users.
